passages.text: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.
passages.sermon: This psalm is for the choirmaster.\r\nThe sons of Korah wrote it.\r\nIt is a Maskil, which means it is a song of wisdom.

passages.text: We have heard with our ears, O God; our fathers have told us the work You did in their days, in the days of old.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
They gave it to the choirmaster.
This psalm is a Maskil, a song of wisdom.
God, we have heard with our own ears.
Our fathers told us what You did.
You worked in their days.
You acted in the days of old.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ לִבְנֵי־ קֹ֬רַח מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃ אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀ בְּאָזְנֵ֬ינוּ שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־ לָ֑נוּ פֹּ֥עַל פָּעַ֥לְתָּ בִֽ֝ימֵיהֶ֗ם בִּ֣ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃

passages.text: With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God used His hand.
God drove out the nations.
God removed those nations from the land.
God planted our fathers in that land.
God crushed the peoples who were there.
God cast those peoples out.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה׀ יָדְךָ֡ גּוֹיִ֣ם ה֭וֹרַשְׁתָּ וַתִּטָּעֵ֑ם תָּרַ֥ע לְ֝אֻמִּ֗ים וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: For it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory. It was by Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You favored them.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel did not take the land by their own sword.
Their own strength did not give them victory.
You, God, gave them the land with Your right hand.
You used Your arm to help them.
The light of Your face shone on them.
You did this because You favored them.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֪א בְחַרְבָּ֡ם יָ֥רְשׁוּ אָ֗רֶץ וּזְרוֹעָם֮ לֹא־ הוֹשִׁ֪יעָ֫ה לָּ֥מוֹ כִּֽי־ יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וּ֭זְרוֹעֲךָ וְא֥וֹר פָּנֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣י רְצִיתָֽם׃

passages.text: You are my King, O God, who ordains victories for Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God is my King.
God rules over all.
God gives commands.
God gives victories to Jacob.
God chooses to save Jacob.
God has power to deliver His people.
God acts for those He favors.
passages.original: אַתָּה־ ה֣וּא מַלְכִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים צַ֝וֵּ֗ה יְשׁוּע֥וֹת יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Through You we repel our foes; through Your name we trample our enemies.
passages.sermon:
God gives us strength.
We defeat our enemies because of God.
We overcome those who oppose us by God's power.
God's name gives us victory over those who rise against us.
passages.original: בְּ֭ךָ צָרֵ֣ינוּ נְנַגֵּ֑חַ בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ֗ נָב֥וּס קָמֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: For I do not trust in my bow, nor does my sword save me.
passages.sermon:
I do not trust in my bow.
My bow does not keep me safe.
My sword does not save me.
I do not rely on my own weapons.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְקַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶבְטָ֑ח וְ֝חַרְבִּ֗י לֹ֣א תוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: For You save us from our enemies; You put those who hate us to shame.
passages.sermon: God saves us from our enemies.\r\nGod puts those who hate us to shame.
passages.original: כִּ֣י ה֭וֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ מִצָּרֵ֑ינוּ וּמְשַׂנְאֵ֥ינוּ הֱבִישֽׁוֹתָ׃

passages.text: In God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever. Selah But You have rejected and humbled us; You no longer go forth with our armies.
passages.sermon:
We praise God all day long.
We boast in God.
We thank God’s name forever.
But God has rejected us.
God has humbled us.
God no longer goes with our armies.
passages.original: בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים הִלַּלְ֣נוּ כָל־ הַיּ֑וֹם וְשִׁמְךָ֓׀ לְעוֹלָ֖ם נוֹדֶ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃ אַף־ זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתַּכְלִימֵ֑נוּ וְלֹא־ תֵ֝צֵ֗א בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: You have made us retreat from the foe, and those who hate us have plundered us.
passages.sermon:
God made us turn back from our enemy.
Our enemies forced us to retreat.
Those who hate us attacked us.
They took what belonged to us.
Our enemies plundered us.
passages.original: תְּשִׁיבֵ֣נוּ אָ֭חוֹר מִנִּי־ צָ֑ר וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֵ֗ינוּ שָׁ֣סוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: You have given us up as sheep to be devoured; You have scattered us among the nations.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God has power over His people.
God has given us up.
We are like sheep ready to be eaten.
God has scattered us.
We are now among many nations.
passages.original: תִּ֭תְּנֵנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן מַאֲכָ֑ל וּ֝בַגּוֹיִ֗ם זֵרִיתָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: You sell Your people for nothing; no profit do You gain from their sale.
passages.sermon:
God acts as the subject in this passage.
God sells His people.
God receives nothing in return.
God gains no profit from their sale.
passages.original: תִּמְכֹּֽר־ עַמְּךָ֥ בְלֹא־ ה֑וֹן וְלֹ֥א־ רִ֝בִּ֗יתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.
passages.sermon:
God has made us a reproach to our neighbors.
Our neighbors look down on us.
People around us mock us.
People around us treat us with scorn.
passages.original: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ חֶ֭רְפָּה לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ לַ֥עַג וָ֝קֶ֗לֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: You have made us a byword among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples.
passages.sermon:
God, You have made us a byword among the nations.
People in every nation use us as an example of disgrace.
You have made us a laughingstock among all peoples.
People everywhere shake their heads at us in scorn.
passages.original: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭שָׁל בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם מְנֽוֹד־ רֹ֝֗אשׁ בַּל־ אֻמִּֽים׃

passages.text: All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame has covered my face, at the voice of the scorner and reviler, because of the enemy, bent on revenge.
passages.sermon:
I feel disgrace all day long.
Shame covers my face.
People scorn me.
People revile me.
My enemy speaks against me.
My enemy seeks revenge.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַ֭יּוֹם כְּלִמָּתִ֣י נֶגְדִּ֑י וּבֹ֖שֶׁת פָּנַ֣י כִּסָּֽתְנִי׃ מִ֭קּוֹל מְחָרֵ֣ף וּמְגַדֵּ֑ף מִפְּנֵ֥י א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּמִתְנַקֵּֽם׃

passages.text: All this has come upon us, though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant.
passages.sermon:
We are the people of Israel.
We have suffered many troubles.
All these troubles have come upon us.
We have not forgotten You, God.
We have not betrayed Your covenant.
passages.original: כָּל־ זֹ֣את בָּ֭אַתְנוּ וְלֹ֣א שְׁכַחֲנ֑וּךָ וְלֹֽא־ שִׁ֝קַּ֗רְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Our hearts have not turned back; our steps have not strayed from Your path.
passages.sermon:
We have not turned our hearts away from You.
We have not let our hearts go backward.
We have not left Your path.
We have not let our steps wander from Your way.
passages.original: לֹא־ נָס֣וֹג אָח֣וֹר לִבֵּ֑נוּ וַתֵּ֥ט אֲשֻׁרֵ֗ינוּ מִנִּ֥י אָרְחֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But You have crushed us in the lair of jackals; You have covered us with deepest darkness.
passages.sermon:
God, You have crushed us.
You did this in a place where jackals live.
You have covered us.
You covered us with deep darkness.
passages.original: כִּ֣י דִ֭כִּיתָנוּ בִּמְק֣וֹם תַּנִּ֑ים וַתְּכַ֖ס עָלֵ֣ינוּ בְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a foreign god, would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart?
passages.sermon:
God knows everything in our hearts.
God sees all secrets inside us.
If we forget God's name, He knows.
If we pray to a foreign god, He knows.
God would discover this.
God understands every hidden thing in our hearts.
passages.original: אִם־ שָׁ֭כַחְנוּ שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּ֝פֵּ֗ינוּ לְאֵ֣ל זָֽר׃ הֲלֹ֣א אֱ֭לֹהִים יַֽחֲקָר־ זֹ֑את כִּֽי־ ה֥וּא יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ תַּעֲלֻמ֥וֹת לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.
passages.sermon: We suffer because of You.\r\nWe face death all day long.\r\nPeople see us as sheep ready for slaughter.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָ֭לֶיךָ הֹרַ֣גְנוּ כָל־ הַיּ֑וֹם נֶ֝חְשַׁ֗בְנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן טִבְחָֽה׃

passages.text: Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever.
passages.sermon:
The people speak to the Lord.
They call God by His name, Lord.
They ask God to wake up.
They say, "Wake up, Lord!"
They ask God, "Why are You sleeping?"
They tell God to arise.
They say, "Arise, Lord!"
They ask God not to reject them forever.
They say, "Do not reject us forever."
passages.original: ע֤וּרָה׀ לָ֖מָּה תִישַׁ֥ן׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י הָ֝קִ֗יצָה אַל־ תִּזְנַ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃

passages.text: Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and oppression?
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
The psalmist asks God a question.
The psalmist says, “Why do You hide Your face?”
The psalmist says, “Why do You forget our affliction?”
The psalmist says, “Why do You forget our oppression?”
passages.original: לָֽמָּה־ פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר תִּשְׁכַּ֖ח עָנְיֵ֣נוּ וְֽלַחֲצֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: For our soul has sunk to the dust; our bodies cling to the earth.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Korah wrote this song.
They sing to God.
They say, “Our soul has sunk to the dust.”
We feel very low and defeated.
Our bodies cling to the earth.
We are crushed and brought down.
passages.original: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה לֶעָפָ֣ר נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ דָּבְקָ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ בִּטְנֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion.
passages.sermon:
God, we call to You now.
We ask You to rise up.
We need Your help.
We ask You to redeem us.
We trust in Your loving devotion.
passages.original: ק֭וּמָֽה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לָּ֑נוּ וּ֝פְדֵ֗נוּ לְמַ֣עַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃
